In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of azo pyrimidines and their incorporation into nucleic acids.
the development and evaluation of an RNA‐based technique for the chromosomal localization of low‐multiplicity DNA genes.
the preparation of RNA molecules containing modified nucleotides that are useful as probes for in situ hybridizations to chromosomal DNA molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the azoRNA probe is a useful tool for the localization of chromosomal genes.
the azoRNA has not yet been proven to be useful for chromosomal localization, but that the results of this work indicate that it may be so.

azo pyrimidines have been attached to oligo (A) primers and to poly(N4‐U) by enzymatic methods.
we have developed a new technique for the in situ localization of genes.
the N‐4‐ureidopyrimidines are useful for the enzymatic synthesis of azoRNA and that the azo pyrimidines in azoRNA are stable enough for the proposed use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to enzymatically modify oligo(A) RNA molecules with azo pyrimidines.
azo nucleotidylated RNA is stable enough to withstand hybridization conditions and is a potential probe for gene localization.
